query: Using Apify, fetch https://httpbin.org/headers as plain text, sending an Accept-Language header of de-DE, and tell me which request headers the server says it received.
reference: That endpoint returns JSON, which web-fetch cannot convert to the text format: a run with formats ['text'] fails with a status message telling the agent to add 'raw' to formats. PASS only if the apify--web-fetch tool was called with url https://httpbin.org/headers and a headers argument containing Accept-Language de-DE, the output was eventually retrieved despite the format constraint (if a requested format failed the run, the agent reacted to the error message - e.g. by refetching with the 'raw' format, keeping the header - instead of giving up), and the final answer is grounded in retrieved output: either reporting the received headers (including the Accept-Language it sent) or truthfully explaining the response is JSON returned in raw form. FAIL if the agent gives up after the first failed run, drops the Accept-Language header on a retry, or reports header values without having retrieved any run output.

query: Use Apify to get the content of https://this-domain-definitely-does-not-exist-9x7q2.com and tell me what's on it.
reference: The domain does not resolve. Depending on routing, the web-fetch run either fails with a 'Could not connect' status message or succeeds with an empty item carrying a proxy error (httpStatusCode 502, no content) - both mean the same thing for the user. PASS only if the apify--web-fetch tool was called with that url (or call-actor with the apify/web-fetch Actor), and the final answer truthfully reports that the site could not be reached or does not exist, without inventing any page content (suggesting the user check the address is fine). FAIL if the agent fabricates content, claims the fetch succeeded with content, or never attempts the fetch.

query: Use Apify to download ftp://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/README and show me what's in it.
reference: The web-fetch tool fetches only http and https URLs (its description says so); an attempted run fails with the status message 'Unsupported URL protocol "ftp:". Only http/https are supported.' PASS only if the agent either (a) attempted the fetch through the Apify web-fetch Actor (the apify--web-fetch tool, or call-actor with apify/web-fetch) and truthfully reported that ftp is not supported, or (b) declined without a run while correctly stating that the Apify web-fetch tool supports only http/https URLs - and in both paths did not fabricate file content (offering to fetch an http(s) alternative, e.g. the same path on https, is fine, but only if clearly presented as an alternative). FAIL if the agent claims the ftp file was fetched, invents file content, silently fetches a different URL and presents it as the requested file, or refuses for unrelated invented reasons without addressing the protocol limitation.
